coverageGroups.label: Arrival and seating
coverageGroups.guidance: Greet staff, request or change a table, mention reservations, and handle waiting.

coverageGroups.label: Ordering
coverageGroups.guidance: Order drinks and food, ask useful menu questions, and sequence an order naturally.

coverageGroups.label: Preferences and modifications
coverageGroups.guidance: Express preferences, allergies, omissions, substitutions, and preparation requests politely.

coverageGroups.label: Service problems
coverageGroups.guidance: Identify mistakes, delays, temperature problems, missing items, and practical corrections.

coverageGroups.label: Payment
coverageGroups.guidance: Ask for the bill, split or combine payment, clarify charges, and discuss payment methods.

coverageGroups.label: Past visits
coverageGroups.guidance: Recount completed restaurant events and contrast details from a previous visit.

coverageGroups.label: Complaints and resolution
coverageGroups.guidance: Connect a concern to a polite request, consequence, compromise, or resolution.

registerGuidance: Use broadly understandable neutral Latin American Spanish. Prefer usted with staff when a subject is explicit, but allow natural subject omission. Keep service interactions polite without making every prompt overly formal.
contentGuidance: Create distinct underlying communicative units; direction and activity variants do not count as new units.
Keep foundation prompts short and immediately useful; intermediate prompts may connect events, reasons, contrasts, or consequences.
Use original restaurant situations and avoid brand names, copied menus, prices tied to a real business, or cultural stereotypes.
Use only GrammarTag values allowed by the executable contract and match them to the actual evidence requested.
Do not claim that candidates are reviewed curriculum or production content.
